explanation.text: The effect of an ion depends on its destination and the proteins it influences. Potassium changes guard-cell water potential, while calcium can trigger either transmitter release or troponin-mediated contraction in different cells.

reasoningChain: Match each ion movement to the stated cell type.
Separate electrical depolarisation, vesicle release and muscle activation.

stem.text: In the nephron of the kidney, selective reabsorption occurs in the cells of the proximal convoluted tubule. Sodium ions are actively transported out of these cells into the surrounding tissue fluid and pass into the blood.
Outline how the active transport of sodium ions out of the proximal convoluted tubule cells results in the absence of glucose in urine.

explanation.text: Sodium pumping maintains a low intracellular sodium concentration. Sodium re-entry down its gradient drives glucose cotransport from the filtrate; glucose then exits towards the blood by facilitated diffusion.
